model_id: OpenAI Codex (GPT-6 family, exact serving revision unverified)

correctness_confidence.basis: For three observations the largest absolute population-standardized deviation is at most sqrt(2). The lower gap is conservative under both SD conventions. In the ASDiv witness, 1200+432 and 1200+464 give the stated margins; 464−(29/27)432 is exactly zero.

rigor.basis: The integer feasibility test uses sorted triples and closed rounding intervals. Two implementations agreed for all raw-score cells. Query weights are common to the two methods; the construction preserves the historical marginal summaries and makes no claim to the observed overlap.

novelty.basis: The inequality and marginal-outcome extremization are classical. The eight cross-order guarantees, attainable ASDiv limit and row-by-row granularity diagnostic are a specific reanalysis. Methodological priority is not demonstrated.

significance.basis: The archived comparison can certify a historical ordering while still permitting a reversal under modest item reweighting. The results inform release design. One model family and eight related mathematics tasks limit external validity.

reproducibility.basis: The manuscript identifies the exact table and repository revision. Results retain file hashes, both precision protocols and integer witnesses. Two clean source checkouts reproduced the same three-page PDF. Individual historical outputs and the actual upstream rounding code remain unavailable in this assessment.

summary: I examined the three rendered pages and the version-specific evidence. The task table and rounding model support a stronger statement than separation of mean accuracies: all nine cross-order comparisons are positive on each task. The ASDiv construction identifies a limit to extrapolating this conclusion to a change of scoring weights. Empty integer cells diagnose the stated reconstruction assumptions; they do not by themselves establish an upstream reporting error. This is appropriate for a working paper.
strengths: States a conservative guarantee independent of whether sample or population deviations were used.
Provides an explicit tie construction with a known question denominator and six realizable run counts.
Retains all tested rounding models and the empty feasible sets.
weaknesses: The weakest 1.06 certificate and the exact 29/27 limit are obtained under different information assumptions. A side-by-side display of those assumptions would aid readers.
No independent reconstruction from historical model outputs was possible.
The externally reported 36-question example does not establish anything empirical about its separate 50-classifier replication.
potential_errors: Filtering or different historical scoring denominators can reconcile empty count sets.
Common question values can be adversarially assigned in the witness; such weights need not correspond to a plausible application.
Extrapolation to new prompt orderings needs a sampling assumption absent here.
strong_novelty_candidates: The attainable 29/27 ASDiv tie threshold tied to explicit integer triples alongside an all-eight-task 1.06 robustness guarantee.
